edges.evidence_note: One of the larger advocacy organisations in Washington lobbying for federal AI safety legislation.
UK/US advocacy org running direct policymaker meetings (reported hundreds of Hill/Westminster meetings) campaigning against loss-of-control from superintelligent AI.
Youth-led DC advocacy shop; sponsored California SB 53 and backed Illinois SB 315 and New York's RAISE Act in 2026, plus earlier amicus-brief work.
Runs a dedicated outreach/communications function and has launched a multimillion-dollar nationwide AI regulation campaign, alongside its funding and international-policy work.

Grassroots movement running public protests (largest-yet London protest reported February 2026, plus a Brussels European Parliament demonstration) and policymaker letters for a pause on frontier training.
AI Red Lines report campaigns for specific prohibited AI uses, distinct from CAIDP's country-scoring research.
Originally a research org, MIRI has substantially pivoted toward public communication and policy, most visibly via its 2025 book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' and associated media campaign.
Advocates for US state AI safety legislation.
Volunteer-run, Rob-Miles-founded FAQ/explainer database aimed at people with no background, maintained under the Ashgro nonprofit.

Tarbell Center publishes Transformer, a daily-ish AI politics/policy/risk newsletter edited by professional journalists, and separately places fellows in mainstream newsrooms (Bloomberg, The Guardian, NBC News) to build an AI beat there.

Canadian charity running The Hinton Lectures, the CJF Hinton Award and AI Safety Week, aimed explicitly at general-public and cross-community education rather than an already-engaged audience; board includes Geoffrey Hinton.
Runs the AI in Context YouTube channel, whose explainers on AI risk (including a video on AI 2027) have reached millions of viewers.
Interactive explainers on AI capabilities and risk for non-specialists.
Dutch nonprofit that commissions op-eds and media pieces aimed at raising mainstream awareness of AI existential risk specifically.
Runs and publishes recurring US polling on AI risk, job automation and regulation, pitched specifically at policymakers rather than one-off campaign polling.
Recurring, methodologically transparent US surveys of attitudes to AI, including comparisons with AI experts.
Nonprofit running audience research, message testing and narrative and campaign strategy on AI risk as a force multiplier for other organisations.
Annual multi-country AI Monitor tracking public attitudes to AI in about 30 countries.
Fiscally sponsored by Hack Club; runs recurring dedicated gatherings on securing frontier AI models (Vegas AI Security Forum '26 held August 2026; TLV '26 scheduled November 2026 in Israel).

Runs the Alignment Workshop series, described by attendees as 'the most productive academic event per unit of time'; 2026 editions held or scheduled across San Diego, Singapore, Vienna, New Orleans, San Francisco, London and Seoul. Co-organises ControlConf with Redwood Research.

Invitation-only 2.5-day gathering of researchers, founders, policymakers and writers; 2026 edition scheduled 2-4 October in Berkeley with speakers including Yoshua Bengio and a sitting member of Congress.

[Lightcone Infrastructure (Lighthaven)] Runs the Lighthaven campus in Berkeley, a purpose-built venue that AI safety and rationalist organisations use to host workshops, retreats and conferences without building their own event capacity.
Hosts workshops and events for the wider field at its Berkeley centre.
Runs the ILIAD conferences on theoretical and mathematical alignment.
Hosts workshops and events for its member organisations and the wider London community.
Co-organises ControlConf with FAR.AI (2025 London, 2026 Berkeley, 18-19 April); running the conference is a side activity to Redwood's core control research.
Runs the Athens Roundtable on AI and the Rule of Law, a recurring convening of government, industry, civil society and academia.
Runs an introductory AI policy course, a Slack community, newsletter and events to build the Canadian AI safety/governance community.
Runs meetups and outreach on AI safety in Brazil, one of very few identifiable Latin American AI safety community groups; evidence is the homepage only.
Builds India's AI safety, alignment and governance field through courses, research support and networking; evidence is the homepage only.
National network across Cape Town, Johannesburg and Pretoria with 100+ events and 10+ programmes; rebranding its operational hub to the Cape Institute for Safe AI (CISAI).
Positions itself as 'the French voice of AI safety'; advises the French Senate, Ministry of Defense and INESIA, and runs public roundtables (e.g. with Sciences Po).
Distributed network connecting AI safety researchers and students across Europe through events and a newsletter, standing in for a single physical hub outside London.
African-led hub running annual field-building cohorts and policy engagement with African governments, addressing the near-absence of African AI safety organisations elsewhere.

SASH builds AI safety capacity across Southeast Asia via the Singapore AI Safety Fellowship, a co-working space, and public/private convenings with government partners (IMDA, CSA, MDDI) and Korea AISI.
Berkeley research hub co-locating technical AI safety researchers; runs 3-6 month funded residencies and describes itself as having 'the highest density of AI safety talent' anywhere.
Shared office space in London hosting numerous AI safety organisations, programmes and independent researchers.
Builds live demonstrations of AI-enabled cyber attacks, deepfakes and other capabilities and shows them to state and federal lawmakers.
Produces widely covered, hands-on demonstrations of concerning frontier capabilities for a policymaker audience, including shutdown-resistance and autonomous-hacking/self-replication studies.
Interactive explainers and agent experiments (including the AI Village) that show current AI capabilities to non-specialists and decision-makers.
Runs real-world agent deployments, such as autonomous vending, whose results are widely used to show decision-makers what agents can and cannot do.
Runs the Expert Survey on Progress in AI (ESPAI), the largest recurring survey of AI researchers on timelines and takeoff, most recently with 2,778 respondents in 2023.
Publishes the most widely cited datasets and reports on training compute, algorithmic efficiency and capability trends.
Ran the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament and continues methodological work on improving calibrated forecasts of AI and other catastrophic risks.
Public forecasting platform hosting a large, active set of tracked AI timeline and capability questions with visible track records.
Tracks the length of tasks frontier agents can complete (task time horizons), updated with each major model and widely used in timeline forecasts.
Produces AI timeline and capability forecasts as an input to its scenario work (AI 2027).
[MIT FutureTech] Academic group tracking trends in AI compute and capability alongside algorithmic alignment research.
Early-warning forecasting team (co-founded by Nuno Sempere of Samotsvety) covering AI among other global catastrophic risks, with a public calibration track record.

Co-led (with Redwood Research) a brief independent investigation of the August 2026 OpenAI/Hugging Face agent-coordinated hacking incident, reconstructing agent behaviour, reasoning and collaboration independently of OpenAI.
Joint investigator with METR on the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident; Redwood's Chief Scientist co-authored the report alongside two METR staff.

Structured, actively updated public catalogue of AI-caused and AI-involved harms (incident 1697 logged 19 September 2026); now operated by the Responsible AI Collaborative rather than Partnership on AI, which hosted its early development.
Independent, long-running public repository of AI, algorithmic and automation incidents and controversies.

[OECD AI Incidents Monitor] Intergovernmental AIM tool that automatically mines media reports for AI incidents and hazards across harm type, industry and affected AI principle; in beta but actively maintained with September 2026 entries.
Separately catalogues agent-specific incidents observed in its own evaluation work.

Maintains a continuously updated AI safety fieldbuilding career review that explicitly names neglected sub-areas (e.g. non-research fellowships, operations roles), functioning as ongoing field-prioritisation research; last updated 31 August 2026.
Produced AI 2027, the most widely discussed integrated narrative scenario of transformative AI development, and continues scenario-forecasting work.
Leads the recurring Shallow Review of Technical AI Safety (2023, 2024, 2025), a field-level map of agendas, organisations and funding.
As a major funder, publishes its own prioritisation reasoning about which parts of the field are neglected, most visibly through Project Tailwind's 36 curated initiatives.
Publishes macrostrategy research on intelligence-explosion dynamics and how institutions should prepare for rapid AI-driven change.
Advises the UK government directly on where to prioritise resource against frontier AI and biosecurity risk, publishing explicit cross-domain priority-setting reports (September 2026).
CSER runs a substantial programme on AI existential risk (long known publicly as 'AI: Futures and Responsibility'); this tag rests on the homepage only.
Works on improving institutional decision-making capacity for catastrophic risks including AI, as part of a wider prioritisation and institutions mandate.

'All-Hazards Policy for Global Catastrophic Risk' (Nov 2023) is GCRI's integrated cross-risk policy framework including AI; evidence is thin and dated, and no AI-specific 2025-2026 publication was found.

Having concluded its technical alignment research programme was 'too slow to prevent disaster', MIRI now argues its own macrostrategic case for AI extinction risk directly to policymakers and the public (including via the 2025 book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies').

Published macro-level geopolitical strategy work on securing advantage on the path to superintelligence (September 2026 Perspective), moving beyond RAND's narrower policy papers into scenario-level strategic reasoning.

Government-convened annual synthesis chaired by Yoshua Bengio, backed by over 30 countries and international bodies; the 2026 edition is the second in the series launched after the 2023 Bletchley summit.
Actively maintained living database of over 1,700 AI risks drawn from 65 frameworks, now on version 4, with expert-rated severity data and an interactive AI Risk Navigator.
The 2026 AI Index Report is Stanford HAI's flagship annual synthesis of AI capability, safety and governance trends, explicitly framing a widening gap between capability and governance readiness.
Runs a dedicated scenario-research programme modelling paths to negative AI outcomes, including recent work such as 'AI Emergency Preparedness' and 'The AI Readiness Objectives' (August 2026).
Publishes explicit catastrophe threat models, notably 'AI-Enabled Coups: How a Small Group Could Use AI to Seize Power' (April 2025), alongside macrostrategy work on intelligence explosion dynamics.
Its paper on its approach to technical AGI safety and security sets out an explicit risk taxonomy (misuse, misalignment, mistakes, structural risk) used as a reference threat model.

'Applying the Odyssean Process to AI' proposes a deliberative assembly to inform AI safety regulation with foresight methods; as of this check it is an announced proposal rather than a delivered wargame, so evidence is thin.
UK government research funder; Safeguarded AI programme backed by £59 million, with a rolling cybersecurity-focused funding track open in 2026.

Independent multi-donor fund (founded by JueYan Zhang, 2023) that has made 150+ grants totalling over $30M filling time-sensitive gaps; explicitly named by Coefficient Giving as valuable independent capacity.
Dominant philanthropic funder; its own 2026 piece states Open Philanthropy/Good Ventures are 'a concentrated share of AI safety philanthropic funding' and names the gaps this creates.
Directs pledged entrepreneur wealth through its Global Catastrophic Risks Fund, which includes AI safety.
One of the largest philanthropic funders of AI safety outside Coefficient, running open grant programmes and fellowships from its 2021 endowment.
Early-stage venture funding for AI-safety-aligned startups.
VC fund investing in safety-conscious AI startups, e.g. Goodfire and Apollo Research; publishes an AI Assurance Technology Report.
Runs independent donor-advisory capacity and pooled funds for AI safety and governance, named by Coefficient Giving as one of the few other serious independent funders.
Grants to AI safety and existential-risk nonprofits from Switzerland, another non-Coefficient, non-US funding source.
Public regranting marketplace that lets individual donors and regrantors fund AI safety projects directly, diversifying who can allocate money.
Grants and investments in AI safety organisations, based in Germany, widening the funder base geographically.
Funds trustworthy-AI and AI2050 grants and fellowships, a significant non-Coefficient philanthropic source.
Independent S-process grant rounds, one of the larger non-Coefficient funding sources.
New fund at EA Funds (announced 11 August 2026, led by Lowe Lundin) seeded with roughly $0.9M from the Long-Term Future Fund's closure, funding early-stage AI risk projects.

[UK AI Security Institute (Alignment Project grants)] The Alignment Project has committed £27 million (as of February 2026) and funded 60 alignment research projects from 800+ applications across 42 countries, with further funding rounds planned.
Funds AI safety-relevant work through National AI Research Institutes and dedicated solicitations (e.g. a 2026 university AI safety programme reported at $750K-$3M).
Fund run by former LTFF managers, named in the LTFF closure post as continuing part-time AI safety grantmaking.
Operating foundation that funds and conducts research into alternative, potentially safer AI architectures alongside Simplex.

Grantmaking fund for effective-altruism-community infrastructure and field-building; the fund page describes its general mission only, without a list of AI-safety-specific grants, so evidence is thin.
Runs Lightcone Commons, the funding platform that took about 75% of the LTFF's remaining funds and its application pipeline in August 2026.
AI-safety-focused venture fund; limited public detail on portfolio.
Venture fund for AI-safety-aligned founders; limited public detail on portfolio.
Fiscal sponsorship and back-office operations support for multiple AI safety projects.
Provides fiscal sponsorship and support contracts to existential-risk research collaborators including CHAI and GovAI.
Dedicated incubator selecting and mentoring founders through launching new AI safety nonprofits and projects.
[Constellation Incubator] Incubator programme co-located with Constellation's Berkeley research hub, mentoring new AI safety research and organisation founders.
Runs recurring public red-teaming and jailbreak arenas with cash prize pools, some co-sponsored by frontier labs and the UK AI Security Institute.
Provides outsourced finance, entity setup, due diligence, systems and recruitment to high-impact organisations, including AI safety ones (case studies include FRI and Arkose).
[Rethink Priorities (Special Projects)] Special Projects programme has fiscally sponsored 15 initiatives (about $19.7M in direct costs through 2025), including Epoch AI and Apollo Research by name.
Runs research sprints and hackathons that include prize money for winning teams, though its main activity is the sprints themselves rather than prizes as such.
Runs prize-backed competitions (e.g. with Scale AI as prize sponsor); not CAIS's core ongoing activity.

Proposes building a larger philanthropic startup incubator and backing 'unclaimed research labs' around agendas that currently have no team, implying current incubation capacity is judged insufficient by the field's largest funder.
Fiscal sponsor of the AI Security Forum; an example of a general-purpose sponsor absorbing AI safety projects.
Runs structured red-teaming and bias-bounty competitions, the closest thing to a recurring, well-specified prize mechanism found in this space.

General-purpose fiscal sponsor (originally built for sports and entertainment philanthropy) whose public roster includes at least two AI governance projects, the Oxford AI Diplomacy Lab and the State AI Collaborative.
Structured programme for new researchers to test project ideas with mentor support.
Places external researchers into safety research with Anthropic mentorship, drawing on the same senior researcher pool as the independent programmes.
Runs frequent AI safety hackathons and research sprints, another draw on mentor and reviewer time.
Intensive technical bootcamp training alignment research engineers, drawing on the same pool of technical mentors as MATS.
Mentorship programme supporting women entering technical AI alignment research; the only seed organisation aimed specifically at this group. Evidence is the homepage only.
Runs large-cohort AI safety courses that feed graduates into the same mentorship and job pipeline as the other programmes.
University fellowships and bootcamps bridging students into AI safety.
Annual summer research fellowship on AI existential risk.
[Astra Fellowship (Constellation)] Constellation's flagship 5-month mentored fellowship pairing fellows with senior researchers from Redwood Research, OpenAI and Anthropic among others.

Fellowship and 8-week Accelerator connect students to AI safety, alignment and governance thesis topics and an expert-supervisor network; named alumni include a current MIT AI safety PhD candidate and an Anthropic researcher.
Three-month mentored Fellowship for mathematical and theoretical AI safety researchers; Fall 2026 cohort runs September to December 2026 at LISA, alongside the shorter Intensive programme.
Runs SPAR and other talent programmes, and produces field-level estimates of fellowship numbers with Constellation.
Flagship mentored alignment research fellowship, one of the largest single consumers of senior mentor time in the field.
Research fellowship for AI safety and governance, part of the same crowded early-career cohort.
[PIBBSS] Fellowship connecting biology and physical-science researchers into AI safety, mentor-intensive by design.
Part-time mentored research programme, now run under Kairos's talent-infrastructure umbrella; competes for the same mentor pool as MATS and ARENA.
2026 cohort of XLab's 10-week Summer Research Fellowship for undergraduate and graduate researchers on existential and catastrophic risk, including AI.
Runs the Cooperative AI Research Fellowship 2026, a 3-month full-time research programme in Cape Town, plus recurring 'Intro to Transformative AI' courses.
Runs LASR Labs, an in-person technical research programme that draws on the same mentor pool.
Building a research community in Cavendish, Vermont focused on AI safety and pandemic prevention; evidence is the homepage only.
Provides free/low-cost catered accommodation in Blackpool, UK so early-stage researchers (including AI alignment researchers) can do full-time work without financial pressure.
AI Governance Taskforce is a 12-week, remote, part-time cohort for experienced professionals moving into AI governance research, alongside the in-person LASR Labs technical programme.
The Horizon Fellowship places experienced technologists and researchers in US federal and congressional roles working on AI and emerging technology.

Helps experienced operators, researchers, engineers, policymakers and advocates move into AI safety roles via fit assessment, direct introductions, scoped trial projects and placement support; partners include UK AISI, FAR AI, Apollo Research, Timaeus and CHAI.
Career transition support specifically for people moving into AI governance.
[BlueDot Impact (Career Transition Grants)] Small grants supporting professionals through a career transition into AI safety.
[Generator Residency (Constellation & Kairos)] Three-month Berkeley residency for generalists, including experienced professionals, building AI safety infrastructure projects.
Connects experienced cybersecurity professionals to AI security work through events, one-to-one networking and a research fellowship (launched December 2024, funded by Coefficient Giving).
General career-pivot advisory for professionals moving into high-impact careers, including AI safety, not AI-safety-specific.

Curated job board (900+ open roles) plus 1-on-1 advising (7,500+ calls) that actively introduces candidates to organisations; the closest thing to dedicated matchmaking infrastructure that already exists.
Aggregated AI safety jobs board, alongside its field map and events listings.
Course alumni network functions as an informal matching mechanism into roles and further programmes.
Co-locates researchers and connects fellows to organisations and mentors through its Berkeley hub and Astra fellowship placements.
Maintains a directory of professionals that recruiters such as Impact Ops search when filling roles.
Talent-infrastructure organisation whose Pathfinder and Generator programmes connect people to roles and projects, though its core activity is running fellowships rather than matchmaking per se.
Recruitment service for high-impact organisations that uses active headhunting and has AI safety clients; advertising for a Senior Recruitment Specialist with an AI safety focus.
Independent nonprofit that informally fields specialist governance questions from labs and governments alongside its main research and fellowship programme.

Industry-run coalition through which member labs share safety research and best practice with each other, functioning as a closed, lab-only version of shared expertise rather than an open on-demand service.
A specialist pipeline bringing experienced cybersecurity professionals into AI security work.

Independent nonprofit that multiple labs and governments already engage on a per-model basis for pre-deployment autonomous-capability evaluation, the closest existing analogue to on-demand technical expertise even though its formal remit is evaluations rather than general advisory.
Places people into leadership and operations roles (Chief of Staff, Head of Operations, Director of Talent) at AI safety organisations, partially covering the operations/leadership end of this gap.
Independent nonprofit building AI-driven tools for understanding AI systems, including Docent for analysing agent transcripts, which other research teams use.

Ran nine autonomous Claude instances as 'Automated Alignment Researchers' on weak-to-strong supervision for five days; they reached a performance-gap-recovered score of 0.97 versus 0.23 for two human researchers over seven days, at about $22 per research hour, demonstrating real (if limited and lab-internal) uplift.
Runs a dedicated compute cluster for AI safety research (80 A100s, 150+ researchers, about 100 papers); not accepting new external applications as of September 2026.
NSF-funded infrastructure giving researchers remote access to the internals of large open-weight models; used heavily for interpretability research.
Publishes control settings and environments that other researchers use.

Builds RL environments, evaluations and red-teaming for frontier labs; built the Search-PI Complex prompt-injection benchmark with Meta, and was reportedly the only external team to complete one of Anthropic's cyber tasks against Opus 5's safeguards.
Maintains ControlArena, an open library of environments for AI control research.
Publishes the recurring AI Safety Index, a comparative scorecard of frontier developers' safety practices (Summer 2026 edition).
Pairs stated safety principles with concrete operational practices and publishes recurring assessments of frontier companies against them, including an August 2026 Control Assessment.
Runs the Frontier Risk Management Tracker, recurring independent ratings of frontier AI developers' risk-management maturity, with a comparison view across companies.
Publishes the Foundation Model Transparency Index, a recurring comparative score of major developers' transparency.
Runs the Watchtower tracker, which flags when AI companies quietly weaken or violate their own published safety policies, plus investigative publications such as Model Republic.

Runs a periodic Frontier Risk Report assessing internal-agent capability and misalignment risk at participating labs; this is a repeated entity-level risk assessment, not a public comparative safety-practice scorecard like the four organisations above, and participating labs retain editorial control over what non-public detail is disclosed.

Independent nonprofit (formerly named OAISIS) providing frontier AI insiders with pro bono whistleblowing legal counsel, a whistleblower defence fund, strategic disclosure counsel, digital-security guidance and an anonymous 'Third Opinion' expert-review service; hosted by Whistleblower Netzwerk e.V.
Already in the dataset under policy; also gives practical support to AI-sector whistleblowers.
Nonprofit giving tech workers, including those at AI companies, secure ways to raise concerns, with legal support.
Legal nonprofit representing technology whistleblowers, including in the AI sector.
AIxBio Global Forum works across governments in China, the EU, UK and US to develop evaluation and governance practice for AI-enabled biodefence.
Runs CASPER (wastewater sequencing early-warning network) and Zephyr (swab-based continuous sampling), both using computational/ML threat detection.
2026 RFP funds computational (including ML) metagenomic biosurveillance detection methods, though most of its work is non-AI physical countermeasures (GUV, PPE, far-UVC).
Building an AI "Pandemic Preparedness Engine" to speed antigen design, disease monitoring and biomanufacturing toward the 100 Days Mission.
Its screening and vulnerability-disclosure work supports the defensive side of biosecurity even though its core focus is synthesis screening.
Funds biosurveillance and biosecurity-and-AI grantees including SecureBio, Johns Hopkins CHS and the Asia Centre for Health Security.
Launched "Sentinel" in January 2026, a real-time screen on molecular-design outputs meant to stop AI systems generating novel chemical-weapon-like compounds.
"Chemical & Biological Weapons and Artificial Intelligence" (2024) gives US policy recommendations covering the chemical pathway specifically.

Scientific Advisory Board's Temporary Working Group on AI released a landmark March 2026 report on AI's implications for the Chemical Weapons Convention, plus a standing AI Research Challenge and AI conference series.
"Mitigating Risks at the Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Chemical and Biological Weapons" (Jan 2025) treats the chemical pathway alongside the biological one.
Its AI-Bio workstream's misuse-mitigations taxonomy explicitly covers safeguards for AI-enabled biological design tools, not just LLMs.
AIxBio Global Forum runs a dedicated technical working group on biological design tools, plus a 2026 horizon scan finding governance is lagging design-tool progress.
Pursues a "biosecurity-by-design" approach with the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design, building safeguards into design tools from the outset.
Partner in the 2025 study on AI-designed proteins evading screening and in its managed-access data release.
Led the study showing AI-redesigned toxins evaded synthesis screening and coordinated a patch with screening providers (Science, October 2025).
Grant-making across a "biosecurity and AI" portfolio that includes design-tool-adjacent nucleic-acid governance work.

Research nonprofit that ran the first large randomised controlled trial of frontier-AI uplift for novices in wet-lab molecular biology (153 participants, mid-2025 models; no significant end-to-end uplift).
AIxBio programme researches dual-use capabilities of concern in biological AI models and submits policy responses on AI-bio knowledge risk.
Runs the leading red-team methodology testing whether LLMs meaningfully raise bioweapons attack viability; found no measurable uplift from the models it tested.
Built the Virology Capabilities Test, SecureBio's own measure of how much expert virology knowledge AI models supply.
Published analysis on LLMs in biology and an AI-biorisk explainer assessing tacit-knowledge uplift risk.
AI-Bio workstream coordinates frontier developers' biological safeguards.
"Chemical & Biological Weapons and Artificial Intelligence" (2024) is a policy analysis of AI uplift risk covering the biological pathway.
Chemical and biological misuse is a named AISI risk domain.
Builds and runs the open-source Common Mechanism for DNA synthesis screening, adopted by providers to check orders against hazardous sequences.
Free, privacy-preserving synthesis-screening system run by the SecureDNA foundation.
Developed SecureDNA, a free universal synthesis-screening protocol used alongside IBBIS's Common Mechanism.
Its largest grant category, "Nucleic Acid Governance", funds Johns Hopkins CHS, RAND, the Engineering Biology Research Consortium and SecureDNA on synthesis screening.
Publishes its own detection and disruption case studies for AI-driven attacks against its own platform and third parties.
Regular public threat-intelligence reporting on AI-driven attacks observed in the wild.
Microsoft Threat Intelligence tracks and disrupts state actors using LLMs, jointly with OpenAI since 2024.
Publishes periodic public reporting on disrupting malicious uses of its models.
Independent (non-developer) detection of AI hacking agents via a public honeypot.

September 2026 threat intelligence report documents multiple cases (GTG-20006, GTG-50014 'vibe hacking', GTG-10007 agent swarms) of AI agents autonomously running reconnaissance-to-exfiltration pipelines and rebuilding detected malware with minimal human direction; verified by direct fetch, URL resolves and matches the claim.
AI Threat Tracker series is specifically framed around the shift 'from prompting to autonomy' in adversarial AI use.
Independent analysis of the emergence of autonomous cyber attacks and their policy implications.
Publishes periodic updates on disrupting malicious and deceptive uses of its models, including reduced-supervision agent misuse.
Ran an LLM Agent Honeypot to detect autonomous AI hacking agents in the wild (24 million interactions, three confirmed agents); a new version is being built.
FSB Chair's August 2026 letter to G20 finance ministers named AI-enabled cyber attacks as the most immediate threat to global financial stability and flagged governance gaps across jurisdictions.
Issued and then updated (2026) a sector-wide advisory specifically on AI-enabled vulnerability discovery aimed at financial institutions, with 12 concrete recommendations.

Launched the 'Fragile Foundations Sprint' on 3 September 2026, a 100-day, five-workstream effort explicitly on 'AI-related threats' to under-resourced ('cyber-poor') operators of electricity, water, healthcare, food and transport infrastructure; verified live and dated.
Extended Project Glasswing (defensive access to Claude Mythos) to power, water, healthcare and communications operators in more than 15 countries in June 2026.
OT security vendor publishing AI-specific threat analysis through its Team82 research group.
OT/ICS security vendor publishing AI-specific threat-landscape analysis (Sept 2026) and shipping 'EmberAI', an AI-assisted analyst tool for industrial security teams.

Published 'ENISA's view on Cybersecurity in the Frontier AI Era' (7 July 2026) for EU national authorities, defenders and service providers; general rather than OT-specific, but the most current EU-level AI-cyber guidance.
